subject: HealthWay POC: MAP, security gating, and hosting choice
messages:
From: Mike Thornton <mike.thornton@healthway.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@healthway.com
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 15:23:00 -0700
Subject: HealthWay POC: MAP + hosting options

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team is excited. We want to get a Mutual Action Plan together so we can lock timing and responsibilities for the POC. A few immediate questions that will affect our timeline and procurement path:

- Do you recommend starting the POC on Redwood Hosted, or should we budget for Dedicated capacity from day one?
- We have PHI in scope — SOC 2 + documented data residency in US-East are non-negotiable. Would that push us toward Dedicated or Private?
- What does a minimal MAP look like (security review, PoC milestones, legal/Procurement signoffs) and realistic time-to-close for each hosting mode?

I attached a first-pass healthway-side MAP spreadsheet (HealthWay_MAP_v3.xlsx) and our compliance checklist. Can your team sketch an internal runbook and commercial delta between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private?

Goal: agree on a hosting mode and sign a SOW/PO by the end of September so we can schedule integration work in October.

Thanks,
Mike
Mike Thornton
VP Ops, HealthWay
Phone: +1 415 555 0199

Attachments: HealthWay_MAP_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB), compliance_checklist.pdf (pdf, 120KB)

From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: Mike Thornton <mike.thornton@healthway.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HealthWay POC: MAP + hosting options

Mike — thanks for the clear ask and the MAP draft. I pulled together our proposed MAP milestones and a short ops/commercial summary below. Putting Karthik, Naomi and Rishi on thread to own technical, commercial and security inputs respectively.

High level recommendation (initial):
- Start the POC on Redwood Hosted (U.S. region) for fastest time-to-value and to validate integration surface (2-week smoke + 2-week workload tests).
- If throughput/latency or data residency requirements tighten after the initial POC, transition to Dedicated (reserved pool) for production — this is a 3–6 week provisioning window depending on commit level.
- Private (VPC / on-prem) is reserved for customers requiring customer-managed control plane or air-gapped environments; expect longer procurement/ops runway (6–10+ weeks) and an enterprise license.

Security gating: Rishi, can you confirm whether Hosted with our US-East SOC2 boundary and KMS integration satisfies HealthWay's PHI needs? If not, outline the delta for Dedicated/Private.

Proposed MAP milestones (baseline hosted-first MAP):
1) Week 0: Kickoff & access — Redwood provides test keys + ingestion guide.
2) Week 1–2: Integration smoke tests + basic policy checks.
3) Week 3: Workload evaluation (latency, token cost) — attach benchmark CSV.
4) Week 4: Security artifacts exchange (SOC2 evidence packet).
5) Week 5: Executive review + optional canary (dedicated lanes) if needed.
6) Week 6: Decision / go-live runway or commit to Dedicated.

Commercial note: Naomi — please confirm hosted vs dedicated delta and whether we can offer a staggered commitment (start hosted, credit toward Dedicated if they commit).

I attached a Redwood-side MAP template and a short ops runbook.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai | +1 650 555 0110

Attachments: Redwood_MAP_template_v1.xlsx (attached by Redwood), onboarding_runbook.pdf

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, Mike Thornton <mike.thornton@healthway.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HealthWay POC: MAP + hosting options

On Mon, Aug 24, 2026 at 09:08 AM Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Mike — thanks for the clear ask and the MAP draft. I pulled together our proposed MAP milestones...

Quick technical addendum from infra:
- Hosted (US-East): immediate provisioning, endpoints available in <24h. Good for functional validation.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pool — recommended if sustained p50 latency <= 120ms at peak qps or if they need tenant isolation for audit reasons. Typical lead time 2–4 weeks if we have available pools; 4–6+ weeks if we need procurement for additional capacity.
- Private: supports VPC peering + self-hosted control plane; required for customers mandating customer KMS/HSM separation or full offline change control.

Attached quick latency sample run I did against a typical HealthWay prompt set. Numbers are synthetic but show Hosted median 95ms token step, Dedicated optimized quantized path ~70ms per step when pinned to performant kernels. See LatencyBenchmarks_8_22.csv attached.

Operational considerations:
- If HealthWay will send PHI, we need an explicit data-flow diagram accepted by their security team and an agreed retention policy (we can support short TTLs on logs).
- We can enable strict KV-cache controls and prefix caching to lower unit cost during evaluation.

Happy to jump on a quick tech walk if Mike wants a live run.

-Karthik
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: LatencyBenchmarks_8_22.csv

From: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, Mike Thornton <mike.thornton@healthway.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HealthWay POC: MAP + hosting options — commercial delta

Thanks team — a short commercial note so procurement has the numbers:

- Hosted (pay-as-you-go): minimal upfront, per-token + per-request billing. Good for POC. Ballpark for HealthWay workload (10M tokens/month on POC) = $Xk/month. (We will provide a detailed estimate once we have real sample traffic.)
- Dedicated (reserved): monthly commit, discounted unit cost and capacity guarantee. Typical commitment: 3–12 months. One-time onboarding fee applies for dedicated pool configuration.
- Private: enterprise licensing + install + optional support retainer. Longer lead-time costs due to network setup and KMS integration.

MAP commercial milestones (suggested):
- Week 0: PO for POC (Hosted credits) or signed SOW for Dedicated evaluation (if they request guaranteed throughput).
- Week 3: Security & procurement checklist complete (SOC2 docs exchanged).
- Week 4: Procurement/Legal sign SOW or issue PO — this is our target to enable Dedicated provisioning if chosen.

HubSpot: I created the deal and attached our MAP as a stage document: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/4721

Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.ai

Mike — summarizing agreed next steps so we have a single source of truth for the MAP and gating items: 

1) Decision path: Hosted-first by default. If during Week 3 workload evaluation HealthWay requests tenant isolation or sustained low-latency SLAs we will present a transition plan to Dedicated (redwood manages provisioning, credits toward commit available). Private reserved for customers that require on-prem or customer-managed KMS.

2) Security gating: Rishi will send SOC2 artifact package and data-flow diagram today (SOC2_evidence_packet.pdf attached). HealthWay security team to confirm retention TTL and KMS requirements by Aug 30.

3) Commercial: Naomi sent a commercial delta. If HealthWay wants marketplace listing and faster procurement, they should sign SOW via DocuSign by Sept 3. Otherwise we can accept a PO for Hosted POC and roll to a Dedicated SOW later.

4) MAP milestones and dates: Kickoff Aug 30 (week 0), integration + smoke tests Sep 1–14, workload evaluation Sep 15–21, procurement/legal decision by Sep 30. Target go/no-go commit date: Oct 7.

5) Attachments: I updated our MAP template and attached the consolidated MAP (HealthWay_MAP_v3—Redwood-edits). Please review and confirm.

Can we get HealthWay to confirm the signoff date (Sept 3 vs Sept 30) for procurement cadence? Naomi — if we offer the marketplace listing window, confirm whether we can hold the offer with a soft reserve.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min sync if that helps.

Cheers,
Soojin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
